behavior.caller_failure_overflow: parser reports overflow: return 0, destination unchanged
behavior.caller_failure_parse: parser returns 0 (empty view or a non-digit first character): return 0, destination unchanged
behavior.caller_failure_trailing: parser succeeds but trailing characters remain (remaining length at [rsp+0x8] != 0): return 0, destination unchanged
behavior.caller_success: parser succeeds and the whole view is consumed: the sum over all levels' records whose +0xb7 byte equals the parsed index is formatted by 0x4faf340 into a temporary string, move-assigned into the destination by 0x514b4f0, and 1 is returned
behavior.caller_success_no_match: a parsed index that matches no record (including any index >= 256, which no zero-extended byte can equal) still returns 1 with the destination set to "0"
behavior.caller_success_no_range_gate: unlike the level-ratio formatter, this caller has NO index-range gate against a level count: the parsed index is compared only against record bytes
behavior.formatter_note: the formatter callee 0x4faf340 converts the 64-bit sum to decimal; its entry thresholds are unsigned compares, so this item pins decimal formatting only for non-negative sums and leaves the sign treatment of a bit-63-set sum as an unknown
behavior.general: given an outer object, a destination string and a (pointer, length) view holding a decimal index, set the destination to the decimal sum of the +0x10 fields of all records whose +0xb7 byte equals that index, and return 1; return 0 without touching the destination when the view is not exactly one decimal index
behavior.move_assign: the temporary string is moved into the destination by 0x514b4f0 (its SSO/heap arms are bound by its own item); the temporary's heap buffer, when present, is then sized-deleted with size capacity + 1 via _ZdlPvm@plt, and the SSO case deletes nothing
behavior.parser_empty: an empty view (length 0) returns 0 and writes 0 to the output slot
behavior.parser_non_digit: a non-digit character stops the scan: the function returns 1 with the accumulated value when at least one digit was consumed, else 0 with value 0; the view struct is left pointing at the stopping character with the remaining length
behavior.parser_overflow: accumulation is checked against UINT64_MAX: value > 0x1999999999999999, or value == 0x1999999999999999 with the next digit > 5, returns 0 without writing the output slot; the view struct keeps the consumption of the digits before the overflowing digit
behavior.parser_rule: scan decimal digits from the view pointer, accumulating value = value * 10 + digit in uint64; stop at the first non-digit or at the end of the view
behavior.sum_empty_level: a level whose begin pointer equals its end pointer contributes nothing
behavior.sum_negative_fields: the sum is a wrapping int64 sum of the +0x10 fields; only non-negative totals are pinned by the formatter note above
behavior.sum_rule: for every level i in 0..count-1, for every record pointer p in the level's (begin, end) span stepping 8 bytes: if the zero-extended byte at [p+0xb7] equals the parsed index, add the int64 at [p+0x10] to the running sum (starting from 0)

call_sites.formatter_call: 0x514dda0 -> 0x4faf340 (rdi = temporary string at rsp+0x20, rsi = sum)
call_sites.move_assign_call: 0x514ddab -> 0x514b4f0 (rdi = destination string, rsi = temporary string at rsp+0x20)
call_sites.parser_call: 0x514dd13 -> 0x54307c0 (rdi = view struct at rsp, rsi = output slot at rsp+0x18)
call_sites.trailing_failure_arm: 0x514dde8 (xor ebp, ebp; jmp cleanup) returns 0 when trailing characters remain

container_layout.count_type: signed int32, sign-extended (movslq); count <= 0 skips the loop
container_layout.span_offsets: begin +0x0, end +0x8 within each level entry

functions.padding: 15 int3 bytes to the next FDE at 0x514de00

integer-to-decimal-string callee, cited as a callee only
string move-assign, bound by its own item; this window is one of its 20 caller sites (0x514ddab, census only there)

the wider semantics of the outer object, the sub-object and the level container beyond the offsets read here
